title: Data Exfiltration and Unauthorized Egress Investigation Playbook
source: MITRE ATT&CK TA0010 (Exfiltration) & NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 / CISA Data Security Guidance
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
Data exfiltration consists of unauthorized transfer of sensitive internal data (intellectual property, PII, financial records, client databases, credentials) from enterprise systems to external attacker-controlled infrastructure. Methods include cloud storage synchronization abuse (e.g., rclone, MEGA, OneDrive, Dropbox), encrypted outbound tunnels (SSH, HTTPS, SFTP), or alternative network protocols (ICMP, DNS). Detection indicators include:
- Abnormal outbound data transfer volume spikes (gigabytes/terabytes) departing a host outside normal business hours.
- Process execution of compression and archiving utilities with encryption/password flags (e.g., 7z.exe a -p, rar.exe a -hp, tar, zip).
- Execution of command-line cloud synchronization tools (e.g., rclone.exe copy, megacmd, curl -F, s3cmd, azcopy) on sensitive file servers or databases.
- Network egress connections to unsanctioned file-sharing, paste sites, or newly spun cloud object storage buckets (AWS S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage).
- Data Loss Prevention (DLP) alerts flagging mass file downloads or transfers containing credit card numbers, Social Security numbers, or confidential document classifications.

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- Network Egress & Firewall Logs: NetFlow / IPFIX / Palo Alto / Fortinet logs capturing source internal IP, destination external IP/port, protocol, bytes transmitted, bytes received, and connection duration.
- Web Proxy & TLS Inspection Logs: HTTP POST / PUT request logs, destination domains, MIME types, and uploaded byte counts to external cloud storage and web services.
- Endpoint Process & Command-Line Logs: Sysmon Event ID 1 / Windows Event ID 4688 capturing archive creation commands, temporary staging directory creation (e.g., C:\ProgramData\, C:\Windows\Temp\, /tmp/), and data transfer commands.
- File System & Storage Audit Logs: Windows File Share auditing (Event ID 5145 - Detailed File Share) and database export logs indicating mass data staging or extraction prior to egress.

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Identify Staged Data: Inspect local disks and shared folders for newly created password-protected zip/7z/tar archives containing structured corporate datasets.
- Destination Infrastructure Analysis: Identify destination IPs, ASNs, hosting providers, or cloud buckets to determine whether the recipient is a sanctioned business partner or attacker infrastructure.
- Impact Assessment: Quantify the total volume, classification level, regulatory compliance implications (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS), and sensitivity of exfiltrated data records.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- Terminate Active Egress Connections: Immediately sever active outbound network sessions and isolate the exfiltrating host via EDR.
- Block Destination Infrastructure: Enforce immediate IP, domain, and URL blocks on perimeter firewalls, proxies, and cloud security gateways.
- Revoke Compromised Credentials: If data exfiltration utilized cloud API keys, service accounts, or user identities, revoke access tokens and rotate all associated secret keys immediately.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Eradicate Staging & Tooling: Remove all staging archives, persistence scripts, scheduled tasks, and unauthorized exfiltration binaries (rclone, curl scripts).
- Implement Egress Filtering & Proxy Enforcement: Restrict direct outbound internet egress from database and application servers; mandate TLS-inspecting proxy routing for all internal clients.
- Deploy Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) & DLP: Restrict personal cloud storage usage on corporate assets and deploy automated DLP policies to block unapproved bulk data uploads.
- Formal Incident Notification: Initiate legal, compliance, and regulatory notification workflows in accordance with data breach disclosure obligations.
